name: Mibolerone (Cheque Drops)
lead: Mibolerone, also called dimethylnortestosterone (DMNT) and sold under the brand names Cheque Drops and Matenon, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from nandrolone. It was marketed by the Upjohn Company as a veterinary drug whose labeled purpose was to suppress estrus (heat) in adult female dogs [1][2]. It is not approved for human use.

In laboratory science, mibolerone is used as a high-affinity androgen receptor ligand in studies of prostate and breast cancer cell lines [3][4]. Outside veterinary and laboratory settings, it is discussed in bodybuilding and strength-sport circles as a very potent oral androgen, and it is a controlled substance in several countries (Schedule III in the United States, Schedule IV in Canada) and prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency [1][2].

No published clinical trial has tested mibolerone in humans for muscle gain, appearance or any other purpose. Claims about its effects on people come from community reports and from extrapolation of its receptor pharmacology.

paras: Mibolerone was approved as an oral veterinary product to prevent estrus in adult female dogs. It acts by inhibiting release of luteinizing hormone from the pituitary, which suppresses ovulation [2]. Experimental use in cats has also been reported [2]. The drug is reported to be no longer commercially available in the United States, with supply limited to compounding pharmacies [2].

Labeled contraindications include pregnancy, lactation, prepubertal animals and impaired liver function. Reported adverse effects in dogs include enlargement of the clitoris, vaginitis and vaginal discharge, and increased sebaceous gland activity [2].

Mibolerone is a 17-alpha-alkylated derivative of nandrolone, a structure that allows oral activity. It binds the androgen receptor with very high affinity and also retains progestogenic activity through the progesterone receptor [1][2]. Sources differ on how its receptor affinity compares with that of metribolone [1].

In research, it has been used as a radioligand-style tool to characterise androgen receptors in human prostate tissue [2], and in androgen-responsive cell lines it alters expression of prostate-specific antigen [2]. A study of breast cancer cell lines used it as a non-metabolizable androgen and found both proliferative and anti-proliferative responses depending on the cell line [4].

No studies found. Mibolerone's human-related research is limited to laboratory work on cell lines and receptor binding, such as studies of androgen effects in human prostate and breast cancer cells [3][4].

According to descriptions of illicit use, mibolerone is taken in bodybuilding and strength circles as an oral pre-training agent, with users reporting short-lived effects on aggression, focus and strength [2]. It is nicknamed by some forum users with terms such as "hulk juice" and is described by advocates as among the most potent oral androgens. Commentators in the same communities have disputed whether short-acting use could produce visible muscle growth. Because of the veterinary origin, products circulating outside regulated channels are of uncertain provenance.

Mibolerone is listed as a controlled substance in the United States (Schedule III), Canada (Schedule IV) and Brazil (Class C5) [1]. WADA prohibits it as an anabolic agent, and anti-doping laboratories detect its metabolites in urine [2].

Adverse effects have been documented in animals, including virilisation of females, reproductive effects and liver changes [2]. For humans, risks are discussed by analogy to other 17-alkylated oral androgens, such as liver strain, adverse lipid changes, suppression of natural testosterone production and virilisation in women; no human safety data specific to mibolerone have been published.

timeline.event: Upjohn markets it as Cheque Drops/Matenon for estrus suppression in dogs [1][2].

lore.intro: In bodybuilding forums, mibolerone is discussed as an exotic, extremely potent oral androgen of veterinary origin, often in the context of pre-workout aggression and strength [2].

claims.claim: Cheque Drops are the strongest oral steroid for strength and aggression.
claims.believers: Proponents point to its very high androgen receptor affinity and describe sharp strength and drive increases in short bursts before lifting or competition [2].
claims.experts: Its receptor binding is documented in laboratory work, but no published human trial has measured strength or behavioural effects [2][3].

claims.claim: Its short action makes it useful as a pre-workout "on demand" compound.
claims.believers: Users say small oral amounts shortly before training give acute mental and performance effects [2].
claims.experts: No pharmacokinetic or performance studies in humans are available; some forum commenters themselves doubt it could build visible muscle [2].

claims.claim: It can be used without the downsides of other oral steroids.
claims.believers: Some users argue the very small quantities involved limit side effects.
claims.experts: Veterinary labelling documents virilisation and liver changes in animals, and anabolic steroids in general carry documented risks; human data for mibolerone are absent [2].

card.summary: A veterinary oral steroid for dogs that circulates in bodybuilding circles as a hyper-potent pre-workout; no human trials exist.
card.note: Controlled substance in several countries; never studied in humans for appearance or performance.

quick.overview:
Mibolerone is a synthetic androgen that Upjohn sold as Cheque Drops to stop female dogs coming into heat. It is not approved for people.

In bodybuilding circles it is described as an extremely potent oral steroid taken for short-term strength and aggression. Those claims come from community reports; no human studies back them.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor very tightly, and also the progesterone receptor. Its 17-alkyl group makes it active when swallowed. In dogs it suppresses luteinizing hormone release, which blocks ovulation.
quick.risks: Animal use is linked to enlarged clitoris, vaginitis and liver changes. Human risks are inferred from other oral steroids, since no human safety data exist. It is controlled in the US, Canada and Brazil and banned in sport.
